1. Executive Summary

The client requests a modern web calculator application equipped with authentication. Anonymous users (“guest login”) can perform calculations and persist up to five records, which are retrievable during their session(s).

2. Key Requirements Breakdown

Functional Requirements

  • Provide a browser-accessible calculator UI (arithmetic operations, clear, reset).
  • Authentication: “Anonymous login” (i.e., no password or profile) tied to a browser session or device identifier.
  • Storage Cap: Per anonymous user, save only the latest 5 calculation expressions and results. Older records must be discarded automatically.
  • View History: User can list and re-run/inspect past calculations.
  • Responsive Design: “Make it modern” implies modern UX (clean look, mobile-first, accessible).

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Performance  Instant feedback on key presses and calculation results; history retrieval <300 ms.
  • Reliability / Availability  Minimal downtime; graceful degradation if storage service unavailable.
  • Security  HTTPS only, secure cookies/headers, input sanitization to prevent XSS.
  • Scalability  Support at least 10 000 concurrent users with no visible latency increase.
  • Compliance  GDPR/CCPA minimal surface: no PII collected beyond a first-party identifier & timestamp.

3. Feasibility Analysis

Complexity Assessment

Medium. A vanilla calculator is trivial, but adding anonymous-session management, capped persistent history, and modern UX raises complexity.

Tech Stack Recommendations (not pre-defined)

  • Frontend: Next.js (React) or SvelteKit for minimal boilerplate & SSR if SEO later, TailwindCSS for “modern” styling.
  • Backend API: Node/Express (TS) or Python/FastAPI, containerised in ECS/Fargate or Cloud Run.
  • Datastore: Redis (expiring keys) or DynamoDB (TTL attribute) to cap to 5 items per anonymous id.
  • Deployment: Vercel pipeline for frontend. Backend behind an API Gateway on AWS or GCP Cloud Run with native TLS.

Potential Challenges

  • Accurate, consistent session handling across incognito windows & cookie resets.
  • Edge caching vs stale history: ensuring 5-record limit remains accurate in multi-region deployment.
  • Balancing modern UI aesthetics with low-JS footprint for quick load times.

4. Risks & Gap Analysis

Missing Elements

  • Signed-up (non-anonymous) user registration vs guest only — unspecified survivability beyond browser cache clear / device change.
  • Business rationale & monetisation model (ads, subscriptions) influencing feature set.
  • Domain and branding guidelines.
  • Service-level objective (SLO) targets for availability & latency.

Business Risks

  • Session ambiguity leading to mixed or lost histories → user frustration / trust issues.
  • Storage + egress costs if user base spikes.

6. Go / No-Go Recommendation

GO. Functional scope is narrow, tech stack is well understood, and all prerequisites can be provisioned quickly. Proceed after finalising the open questions listed below.

Unanswered Questions to Resolve before Sprint 1

  1. Can sessions persist across device changes or only single-browser?
  2. Is permanent signed-up mode planned later, or will it stay guest-only?
  3. Specific latency & uptime targets (SLAs)?
